{{Short description|British physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2017}}
{{Use British English|date=November 2017}}
'''Stuart Palmer''' FREng, also known as '''S. B. Palmer''', was the honorary secretary of the [[Institute of Physics]],<ref name=iopcouncil>{{cite web|title=Council|url=http://www.iop.org/about/governance/council/page_38744.html|website=Institute of Physics|accessdate=14 January 2015}}</ref> and was the [[deputy vice-chancellor]] of the [[University of Warwick]] between 1999 and 2009. He is an emeritus professor of [[physics]] at Warwick who has worked in [[condensed matter physics]] and [[engineering physics]] and has extensively exploited the technique of [[ultrasound]].

Palmer was born in [[Ilkeston]], [[Derbyshire]], studied at [[Sheffield University]] and spent 20 years at [[Hull University]] before moving to Warwick in 1987, where he was head of the physics department for 12 years.

While working at the [[University of Hull]] he led a team applying ultrasound to the diagnosis and monitoring of [[osteoporosis]].<ref name="PorterPalmer1984">{{cite journal|last1=Porter|first1=R W|last2=Palmer|first2=S B|last3=Langton|first3=C M|title=The measurement of broadband ultrasonic attenuation in cancellous bone|journal= Engineering in Medicine|volume=13|issue=2|year=1984|pages=89–91|issn=0046-2039|doi=10.1243/EMED_JOUR_1984_013_022_02|pmid=6540216}}</ref> This led to an ultrasonic index for osteoporosis<ref name="pmid2224217">{{cite journal|vauthors=Porter RW, Miller CG, Grainger D, Palmer SB|title=Prediction of hip fracture in elderly women: a prospective study.|journal=BMJ|year=1990|volume=301|issue=6753|pages=638–41|pmid=2224217|doi=10.1136/bmj.301.6753.638|pmc=1663899}}</ref> and the development of commercial ultrasound heel scanners that are available worldwide.<ref name="StrelitzkiClarke1996">{{cite journal|last1=Strelitzki|first1=R.|last2=Clarke|first2=A. J.|last3=Truscott|first3=J. G.|last4=Evans|first4=J. A.|title=Ultrasonic measurement: An evaluation of three heel bone scanners compared with a bench-top system|journal=Osteoporosis International|volume=6|issue=6|year=1996|pages=471–479|issn=0937-941X|doi=10.1007/BF01629580|pmid=9116393|s2cid=26081955}}</ref>

More recently{{when|date=October 2026}}, he has developed techniques for the non-contact generation and detection of ultrasound based on both [[laser]] and electromagnetic techniques which have found a wide range of industrial applications.<ref name="ScrubyDewhurst1980">{{cite journal|last1=Scruby|first1=C. B.|last2=Dewhurst|first2=R. J.|last3=Hutchins|first3=D. A.|last4=Palmer|first4=S. B.|title=Quantitative studies of thermally generated elastic waves in laser-irradiated metals|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|volume=51|issue=12|year=1980|pages=6210|issn=0021-8979|doi=10.1063/1.327601|bibcode=1980JAP....51.6210S}}</ref><ref name="Dewhurst1982">{{cite journal|last1=Dewhurst|first1=R. J.|title=Quantitative measurements of laser-generated acoustic waveforms|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|volume=53|issue=6|year=1982|pages=4064–4071|issn=0021-8979|doi=10.1063/1.331270|bibcode=1982JAP....53.4064D}}</ref><ref name="DaviesEdwards1993">{{cite journal|last1=Davies|first1=S J|last2=Edwards|first2=C|last3=Taylor|first3=G S|last4=Palmer|first4=S B|title=Laser-generated ultrasound: its properties, mechanisms and multifarious applications|journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics|volume=26|issue=3|year=1993|pages=329–348|issn=0022-3727|doi=10.1088/0022-3727/26/3/001|bibcode=1993JPhD...26..329D|s2cid=17358514|url=https://semanticscholar.org/paper/ca0abbc3d4282221a90217157ae9401405f2c0fd}}</ref><ref name="BaakliniEdwards2000">{{cite book|last1=Baaklini|first1=George Y.|title=Nondestructive Evaluation of Aging Materials and Composites IV|last2=Edwards|first2=Christopher|last3=Stratoudaki|first3=Theodosia|last4=Dixon|first4=Stephen|last5=Palmer|first5=Stuart B.|last6=Nove|first6=Carol A.|last7=Boltz|first7=Eric S.|editor1-first=George Y|editor1-last=Baaklini|editor2-first=Carol A|editor2-last=Nove|editor3-first=Eric S|editor3-last=Boltz|chapter=Noncontact ultrasound studies of composite materials: New developments|journal=Proceedings of SPIE|volume=3993|year=2000|pages=268–275|issn=0277-786X|doi=10.1117/12.385498|s2cid=138019031}}</ref>

His most esoteric discovery, with Jose Baruchel of ILL and ESRF in [[Grenoble, France]], is the existence of helical or chirality magnetic domains in certain antiferromagnetic materials.<ref name="BaruchelAubert1986">{{cite journal|last1=Baruchel|first1=J.|last2=Aubert|first2=G.|last3=Palmer|first3=S.B.|last4=Schlenker|first4=M.|title=Observation of ferro-helimagnetic phase coexistence in Tb crystals|journal=Journal of Magnetism and Magnetic Materials|volume=54–57|year=1986|pages=1631–1632|issn=0304-8853|doi=10.1016/0304-8853(86)90954-6|bibcode=1986JMMM...54.1631B}}</ref>

In addition to his role as honorary secretary of the Institute of Physics, he chaired the board of the Institute of Physics Publishing and the TRAC Development Group of the Higher Education Funding Council for England (2004-2015). He was a visiting professor at [[Queensland University of Technology]] in [[Brisbane, Australia]] (2014-18), and Chaired the Council of [[Cardiff University]] (2014-22) in the UK. He was secretary general of [[IUPAP]] from 2012 to 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=NEWS BULLETIN, July 2013|url=http://archive.iupap.org/bulletins/file_60595.pdf|website=IUPAP archive|accessdate=14 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Executive Council: Officers Archive 2002-2014|url=http://iupap.org/about-us/executive-council/executive-council-officers-2014-2017/officers-archive-october-2002-2014/|website=IUPAP|accessdate=14 January 2015|archive-date=20 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120023943/http://iupap.org/about-us/executive-council/executive-council-officers-2014-2017/officers-archive-october-2002-2014/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and Hon Treasurer of EPS from 2019-2024.

He was appointed Chair of Council at Brunel University of London in 2022, Trustee of UCEA in 2017 and Deputy Chair of UCEA in 2024.

In 2005, a [[Hull Trains]] [[British Rail Class 222|Class 222]] was named 'Professor Stuart Palmer' in his honour.<ref name="hulltrains">{{cite web|title=Train Named After University of Warwick Deputy Vice-Chancellor|url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/newsandevents/pressreleases/ne1000000110215/|website=University of Warwick|accessdate=14 January 2015}}</ref> He became a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering in 2000 and an Honorary Fellow of the Institute of Physics in 2026.

In 2018, he won the [[Phillips Award]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/phillips/medallists/page_59232.html|title=Phillips Award recipients|accessdate=22 December 2019}}</ref>
